correctness.rationale: Antiderivative tests in each coordinate give the three conditional laws. Stationarity of \(y\) and \(z\) yields \(\mathbb E[y(y+b)]=0\), hence the circle law. Jensen gives \(0\le\theta\le1\) and the variance parabola. Endpoint and slab rigidity follow from invariant support and the sign of \(y(y+b)\). The actual frozen verify.py was read and confirms the core generator and equilibrium identities.

value.rationale: Sprott P is a canonical multistability testbed. The theorem gives an attractor-independent exact moment circle, complete mean–variance curve and a sharp two-sided slab occupation constraint across all compact stationary components.
value.risk: The occupation result is qualitative and gives no lower bound on either mass fraction.

final_claim: For generalized Sprott P with \(b>0\), every compact invariant probability measure satisfies the three coordinatewise conditional stationary laws, the exact circle identity \(\mathbb E[(y+b/2)^2]=b^2/4\), the mean–variance parabola \(\operatorname{Var}(y)=b^2\theta(1-\theta)\), equilibrium rigidity at \(\theta=0,1\), and two-sided occupation of the equilibrium slab for every non-equilibrium-mixture stationary state.
limitations: Periodic-orbit localization is not claimed as new.
The 2004 broad analytical paper remains a literature-access risk.
